substantive_reconstruction.irrational_and_moving_grid: Let t=1/sqrt(2), r=(t,1-t); it is ordered/full rank because1>t>1/2. Every finite lambda_i/n is rational, so equality is impossible and Pr(hat r!=r)=1. For sufficiently large n, lambda^(n)=(floor(nt),n-floor(nt)) is ordered, its normalized vector approaches r and never equals it; KL tends to0 by continuity on a full-rank target. This disproves a uniform positive punctured-simplex gap. The rational r=(1/2,1/2) example on odd n independently shows rationality alone does not fix the universal equality limit.
substantive_reconstruction.support_face_and_gap: Use zero-p terms0 and D infinity when p gives positive weight to a zero r_i. The stipulated single-outcome bound then forces that outcome weight0. On the remaining support face F, all relevant r_i are positive and p log p is continuously extended by0, so D is continuous. F intersect {||p-r||_1>=epsilon} is compact; if nonempty its minimum is positive because D vanishes only at r and epsilon>0 excludes r. If empty, the outside event has probability0. This handles all zero-spectrum cases without assuming full rank or compactness of an incorrectly punctured domain.
substantive_reconstruction.union_and_constants: With h=d(d-1)/2, at most(n+1)^d padded diagrams exist. Summing the given bound over epsilon-away supported diagrams yields Pr(||hat r-r||_1>=epsilon)<=(n+1)^(h+d)exp(-n delta_epsilon). Both factors are necessary in this argument; h+d=d(d+1)/2. Natural-log Pinsker gives D>=||p-r||_1^2/2 (since TV=||p-r||_1/2), so the explicit bound(n+1)^[d(d+1)/2]exp(-n epsilon^2/2) is correct, including incompatible supports with zero weight. This says neither that an exact matching diagram eventually exists nor that any one nearby atom keeps a positive limiting mass. At d1 the only diagram(n) matches r1; for rank-one sorted r at larger d only lambda=(n,0,...) can have positive weight by the same bound.
